candidates.title: Claude Code 2.1.288 closes fail-open permission gaps around shell deletion and hooks
candidates.summary: Anthropic released Claude Code 2.1.288 with permission hardening for dangerous shell deletion and hook failures, alongside reliability fixes for long-running and resumed sessions.
candidates.what_changed: The release now prompts before a dangerous rm embedded inside bash -c or sh -c when bypassPermissions mode or a shell allow rule would previously let it run without a prompt. It also blocks tool calls when PreToolUse or PermissionRequest hook matching fails or tool input cannot be serialized, rather than skipping those hooks.
candidates.why_it_matters: Coding-agent safety depends on enforcement at execution boundaries, not just model intent. Wrapper commands and hook-processing failures are exactly the kinds of edge cases that can turn a nominal permission policy into a fail-open control.
candidates.engineer_takeaway: If your team uses Claude Code with bypassPermissions, shell allow rules, or custom permission hooks, upgrade and test the enforcement path with adversarial wrapper commands and hook failures; keep bypass modes inside isolated environments rather than treating them as a normal workstation policy.

evidence.rationale: Anthropic's immutable v2.1.288 release notes document the dangerous-rm and fail-closed hook fixes. Independent reporting describes the rm wrapper reproduction and affected permission modes; no independent reproduction was performed in this run.
evidence.independent_validation: Independent reporting corroborates the rm wrapper failure and release fix; this orchestration run did not execute a live exploit or regression test.
evidence.claim_scope: The story treats the fixed behavior and release timing as primary-source facts and does not claim broader permission-system safety beyond the documented fixes.

signal.rationale: The fixes affect the permission boundary of a widely used coding agent, including configurations explicitly used for unattended or low-friction execution.

watchlist.title: Claude Mods open a deeper, unsandboxed extension surface inside Claude Code
watchlist.summary: Claude Code 2.1.287 introduced Claude Mods, allowing plugins to modify deeper behavior. The repository source and documentation expose a materially more powerful extension surface, but this controlled run prioritizes the following day's concrete permission-boundary fixes and avoids splitting one rapidly evolving Claude Code release sequence into multiple stories without a stronger independent deployment signal.

evidence.rationale: Anthropic's release feed and public Mods source document the feature; community reporting discusses the security implications.

signal.rationale: A deeper plugin execution surface changes the trust model for coding-agent extensions.
